note: Seed for logs/hosts.json: where this board's projects keep their branches and pull requests. The live file (logs/hosts.json) overrides this one per host id and per project, and is the one the reader edits. docs/hosts.md explains the tokens, the api block and the landing doctrine.

github.landing:
This repo lives on GitHub and main is protected: a branch lands through a pull request, never a push to main.

1. Push the branch, never {main}:  git push -u origin {branch}
2. Open ONE pull request from {branch} into {main}:
     gh pr create --base {main} --head {branch} --title "<a subject a reviewer can read>" --body-file <a file written outside the repo>
   --fill drops the reason a version bump gave, so when this branch carries a bump, pass --title and --body-file and put the
   level and its reason into the body.
3. Read it back before reporting it: gh pr view <n> --json state,headRefOid,baseRefName, and confirm headRefOid is the
   commit you just pushed.
4. Report the PR URL and leave it OPEN. The reader merges it. Do not merge it, do not push {main}, and do not open a
   second PR for the same branch.
5. If the PR is already open and its base moved, rebase onto origin/{main} and push --force-with-lease. That rewrite is
   the only one allowed on a published branch, and only for the PR this run opened.

sefl-bitbucket.landing:
This repo lives on SEFL Bitbucket (git.sefl.com). {main} is not yours to push: a change lands by opening a pull request into {main} and letting a human reviewer merge it.

1. Push the branch, never {main}:  git push origin {branch}
2. Open ONE pull request, {branch} -> {main}, and get all three of these right, because the review queue filters on them:
   - title: "Java Code Review for <repo> <branch>"
   - reviewers: the GROUP code_review_java and nothing else - no individuals, no code_review_java_dal on a non-DAL change
   - description, four sections, every one of them present:
       ## Jira Ticket              the ticket id only, or "none"
       ## Description              what changed and why, in a reviewer's terms
       ## Test Procedures          the commands actually run and their real results - counts, not adjectives
       ## Technical Specifications Confluence links, or the one line saying none applies
   POST it to {base}/rest/api/1.0/projects/{projectKey}/repos/{repoSlug}/pull-requests with
   Authorization: Bearer $BITBUCKET_SEFL_TOKEN (never echo the token), fromRef refs/heads/{branch}, toRef refs/heads/{main}.
   Read the PR back: reviewers must be exactly [code_review_java] and fromRef.latestCommit must be the head you pushed.
   (Repository automation can push to the branch on its own schedule, so if latestCommit is a commit you did not write,
   fetch it, say what it is, and diff it against {main} rather than reporting the SHA you aimed at.)
3. A human reviewer may take a day, and sometimes longer. That is the normal wait, not a failure: report the PR id and
   its URL and stop there. Do not merge it, do not decline it, do not close it, do not push {main}, and do not sit in a
   loop waiting for a person.
4. Once the PR is open, poll it HOURLY - not more often - and answer what arrives:
     GET {base}/rest/api/1.0/projects/{projectKey}/repos/{repoSlug}/pull-requests/<id>/activities?limit=100
   Look for COMMENTED / REVIEWED / UNAPPROVED / MERGED events newer than your last poll. For each comment, make the
   smallest change that answers it, commit on {branch}, push, and reply on that comment naming the commit. An approval
   at an older commit is not an approval of the head: after any push, compare reviewers[].lastReviewedCommit with
   fromRef.latestCommit and say plainly that the head needs re-approval.
5. "Landed" on this host means: branch pushed, PR open, waiting for a human. Say exactly that and quote the PR URL.
   Never report it as merged, and never call the work blocked because a reviewer has not looked yet.
